title: GPU Pool Operational Playbook Cards: compact health + action surface for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, card-based "playbook" surface for each Dedicated GPU pool that surfaces health signals, suggested corrective actions, and one-click controls (canary, burst, scale-to-zero) without sending users into deep drilldowns. The goal is to reduce mean-time-to-action for on-call and platform engineers and give PMs a quick at-a-glance operational posture for billing-sensitive pools.

What this includes (prototype scope):
- Card header: pool name, region, SLA tier, last-seen leader metrics (99th p99 latency, active streams, GPU utilization).
- Health ribbon: color-coded summary (OK, Degraded, Critical) with short reason text and time-since-change.
- Suggested actions panel: autogenerated recommended actions from heuristics (e.g., increase min replicas, enable burst, fall back to cheaper variant) with projected cost delta and reliability impact.
- Quick controls: burst slider (0-100% extra capacity), emergency scale button, start canary rollout button, and a 'freeze' toggle to pin model version. Controls include lightweight confirmations and undo.
- Audit & trace links: quick link to last deployment trace, recent errors, and cost breakdown for the pool in the last 24h.
- Accessibility: ensure color contrast, keyboard focus order for action buttons, and screen-reader labels for health reasons.

Design rationale and trade-offs:
- Card-first vs. panel-first: Card gives scannability on the fleet view and allows grouping by region or SLA. Tradeoff is limited space for dense telemetry; detailed charts live in pool detail page (linked).
- Suggested actions automation: keep heuristics conservative to avoid action noise. We expose projected cost delta to help operators weight decisions and require explicit confirmation for cost-increasing actions.
- Bursting UX: use a subtle slider to set a burst budget instead of immediate hard scaling to encourage measured use; provide a cost guardrail and estimated spend cap.

Prototype artifacts and links (Figma/Drive/Confluence):
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Console-Playbook-Cards-Prototype (frame: Playbook-Cards-v2)
updates: 2026-02-20: Initial design brief and research plan created. Identified common operator pain points from on-call interviews (5 ops engineers).

2026-02-25: Low-fi wireframes validated in 3 contextual interviews. Operators liked one-click actions but raised cost safety concerns. Updated interaction to require preview of cost impact before commit.
2026-03-02: High-fi prototype built in Figma; accessibility pass for color and focus order completed.

2026-03-08: Review with PM and Eng. ENG feedback: need telemetry API for 'projected cost delta' and a feature flag for conservative rollout. Added dependencies ENG-9012 (telemetry schema) and ENG-9041 (control API endpoints).
2026-03-12: Design review session with Solutions Eng and Customer Success. Action: add 'recent autotune suggestions' slot and a collapsible timeline of SLO breaches. Preparing handoff package.
notes: Include a non-blocking 'preview cost' modal that shows estimated spend over 24h/7d for chosen burst budget.
Fallback design: if telemetry API unavailable, disable suggested actions and show 'Telemetry offline' helper state.
Prefer semantic color tokens from design system; map health states to tokens to centralize theming.
Accessibility: ensure the burst slider exposes numeric value to screen readers and can be adjusted via keyboard arrow keys.
next_steps: Finalize interaction spec and atomic components (health ribbon, action chip, burst slider)
Partner with ENG-9012 to finalize telemetry schema for projected cost and anomaly reasons
Schedule handoff meeting week of 2026-03-16 and create JIRA cards for components
blocked_reason: Waiting on ENG-9012 schema sign-off for projected cost delta; without it, suggested-actions must be disabled in prod.
